notes:
PRIMARY REQUESTED MOVE (attempt 1): PASS functionally. 765883 (copy-of-__mcp-probe-subfolder-20260921, 2 cases, no subfolders, the newest and least-depended-on of 765811's two children) moved cleanly from under 765811 to project root. Verified on both ends via the response body and an independent get_folder_tree_v1 re-read: identical counts, identical parentage. 765811 now holds only 765817 as a child (sub_folders_count 2->1); its own 2 direct cases were untouched. No case data was touched by this call, only folder parentage.

THE CYCLE TEST - HIGH-VALUE RESULT: attempted to move 765811 into its own direct child 765817. Got a clean 400 {success:false, error:null, message:null} and confirmed via independent re-read that NOTHING moved - 765811 stayed root-level, 765817 stayed its only child, no orphaning, no corruption. This is the 'right answer' the task asked us to hope for. BUT it directly contradicts this same capability's own stored guidance text, which reads (verbatim, from describeCapability): 'Moving a folder into one of its own descendants is NOT blocked. The only self-move check compares the folder id to the destination id, so a move into a child is accepted here (the copy endpoint does check for this - the move endpoint does not).' Live behavior on preprod today says otherwise: the destination-is-a-descendant case IS blocked, just with an uninformative null/null 400 body instead of a real message. Either the guidance was written against stale/incorrect analysis, or backend behavior changed since it was authored, or the check fires for a reason distinct from what the doc describes (e.g. a generic ancestry-cycle guard rather than the narrow 'folder id == destination id' comparison the doc describes) - in any case, THE GUIDANCE ITSELF IS NOW FALSIFIED BY A LIVE CALL and should be corrected at the capability-index source (not done here per instruction not to edit the index directly) rather than trusted as-is. This is arguably a more valuable finding than either a clean accept or a clean reject alone would have been: it shows the index's own defect-tracking text can go stale/wrong, not just the API.

BAD DESTINATION ID (attempt 3): 999999999 as new_base_folder_id got a 422 {success:false, error:'Destination folder not found in the specified project'} - clean, specific, and correctly worded. This is the fourth distinct bad-folder-id behavior on record for the campaign (alongside create_bulk_test_cases_v1's silent-200-discard, bulk_move_test_cases's generic 400, and bulk_assign_test_cases_to_test_run's undeclared 502) and by far the best-behaved of the four.

GROUP_ID TYPE QUESTION (settled, third data point): this capability - a mutation route like rename_folder_v1 and bulk_move_test_cases - returned group_id as the STRING "3452" in every location it appeared (data.folder, source_path_folders[], destination_path_folders[]). create_sub_folder_v1 (a creation route) returned it as a plain integer for the same folder family. This is now a 3-for-3 pattern: string form on mutation-serializer responses (rename, bulk-move, and now move), integer form on the creation serializer (create_sub_folder_v1). Strongly supports the hypothesis that the string form belongs to the mutation serializers specifically, not to some fields-are-sometimes-strings general inconsistency.

EMBEDDED data.project LEAK (settled, does NOT recur here): move_folder_v1's response - data.folder, source_path_folders[], destination_path_folders[] - carries no project object anywhere. This confirms the leaky embedded project (4 declared fields missing / 16 undeclared, previously found only on create_root_folder_v1) stays confined to that one capability; sub-folder creation, rename, and now move all correctly omit it.

COUNTS ACCURACY (third and settling confirmation): cases_count / sub_folders_count / total_cases_count on old parent (765811), new parent (project root, i.e. no parent object to check but the moved folder's own counts), and the moved folder (765883) were all internally consistent between the move response and an independent get_folder_tree_v1 read taken right after, with the arithmetic checking out (765811: 2 own cases + 2 from remaining child 765817 = total_cases_count 4). Counts can now be treated as reliable across all three capabilities where this has been checked.

SHARED-TEMPLATE 'name must be wrapped' DEFECT - NOT APPLICABLE HERE: move_folder_v1 has no `name` field in its body contract at all (its writable fields are new_base_folder_id, new_base_project_id, auto_rename, prev, next) - there is nothing for the false wrapped-object sentence to attach to, so this is not a fourth instance, just a capability the defect cannot occur on.

RESIDUAL STATE: 765883 now sits at project root (2 cases, no subfolders) instead of under 765811 - this was the intended, requested move and is left as-is, not reverted. 765811 keeps 765817 as its only child. No corrupting state was created (the one operation that could have corrupted the tree - the cycle attempt - was rejected, so no revert-the-cycle step was needed). No case data, other folders (764093, 764138, 764828 and its evidence case TC-54458), or unrelated probe folders under 764138 were touched.

No status:0 was seen on any call; all three real attempts and both tree re-reads returned clean, distinguishable HTTP statuses (200/400/422/200/200). No retry-on-outage situation arose, so the 3-attempt cap was not exercised as a retry budget - all three attempts were distinct, deliberate experiments, not retries of one failing call.
